seoDescription: Learn to streamline your Flask web development by mastering template inheritance and integrating Bootstrap. This tutorial demonstrates how to create a `base.html` template to define common elements like a navigation bar, preventing code repetition across your site. Discover how child templates can extend this base and override specific blocks for dynamic content. You'll also walk through adding Bootstrap's CSS and JavaScript to your Flask project, allowing you to quickly incorporate professional, responsive designs.

chapters.title: Introduction to Template Inheritance
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the concept of template inheritance in Flask and explains how it helps avoid repeating code for common website elements.

chapters.title: Creating the Base Template
chapters.description: Learn how to set up a `base.html` file that will serve as the parent template for all other pages on the website.

chapters.title: Defining & Overriding Template Blocks
chapters.description: This chapter covers how to define replaceable sections called 'blocks' in the base template and then override them in child templates.

chapters.title: Creating Content Blocks and Enabling Debug Mode
chapters.description: Learn how to define a main content block for page-specific HTML and enable Flask's debug mode for automatic server reloading.

chapters.title: Testing the Inherited Template
chapters.description: Run the Flask application to see how the child template successfully inherits code from the base template and displays the overridden content.

chapters.title: Integrating Bootstrap CSS & JavaScript
chapters.description: This chapter walks through adding the Bootstrap framework to the project by linking its CSS and JavaScript files from a CDN.

chapters.title: Adding a Bootstrap Navbar
chapters.description: Learn how to copy a pre-built navbar component from the Bootstrap documentation and add it to the base template so it appears on every page.

chapters.title: Verifying Inheritance with a New Page
chapters.description: Confirm that template inheritance is working by creating a second page that extends the base template and automatically displays the navbar.

summary:
## Template Inheritance in Flask

Template inheritance allows you to build a base "skeleton" template that contains all the common elements of your site and define **blocks** that child templates can override.

- **Base Template (`base.html`)**: Contains the main HTML structure (`<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>`), shared elements like navbars or footers, and defines blocks.
- **Child Templates (`index.html`, etc.)**: Use `extends` to inherit from the base template and then fill in the defined blocks with their own specific content.

### Key Jinja2 Syntax

- `{% extends 'base.html' %}`: Must be the very first line in a child template. It tells Jinja to inherit from `base.html`.
- `{% block title %}{% endblock %}`: Defines a block named `title` in the base template. Child templates can override this section.
- `{% block content %}{% endblock %}`: In a child template, this syntax is used to insert content into the corresponding block defined in the parent.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A child template does not need to define every block from its parent. If a block is not overridden, the content from the parent template (if any) is used instead.

## Integrating Bootstrap

Bootstrap is a popular CSS framework for building responsive, professional-looking websites quickly. You can add it to your Flask project without downloading any files by using a CDN (Content Delivery Network).

### Setup Process

1.  **Add CSS**: In your `base.html` file, copy the `<link>` tag for the Bootstrap CSS and place it inside the `<head>` tag, preferably before any other stylesheets.
2.  **Add JavaScript**: Copy the `<script>` tags for Bootstrap's JavaScript (which may include Popper.js and jQuery) and place them at the very end of the `<body>` tag. This ensures the page content loads before the scripts, improving performance.

> [!TIP]
> Once Bootstrap is added to `base.html`, you can copy and paste components like navbars directly from the Bootstrap documentation into your template. Since all other pages extend `base.html`, they will all automatically get the Bootstrap styling and components.

## Flask Development Workflow

To make development faster, you can enable Flask's built-in debug mode.

### Automatic Server Reloading

- In your main Python file, modify the `app.run()` call:

  `app.run(debug=True)`

> [!NOTE]
> When **debug mode** is active, the Flask development server will automatically reload whenever you save a change to your Python or template files. This saves you from having to manually stop and restart the server after every code modification.
